title: SLO lease transfers and graceful traffic atrophy policy for model endpoints
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Context: Redwood runs model endpoints across regions and model variants with different cost/latency characteristics. Teams have expressed the need for a formal mechanism to temporarily 'lease' SLO headroom from lower-priority routes/variants to keep customer-critical routes online during short spikes, then return or rebalance that lease without causing cascading failures. This ticket defines a policy and operational plan for SLO lease transfers and a complementary 'graceful traffic atrophy' (GTA) strategy that intentionally sheds low-value traffic in an observable, reversible way.
background_and_problem_statement: We currently rely on coarse regional failover and global circuit breakers. When a high-priority route exhausts its error budget or regional capacity, operators often perform manual mitigations (e.g., reduce batch sizes, manual model fallback, or broad rate-limiting) that impact many customers. There is no standardized, auditable process for temporarily borrowing error budget or capacity between routes or regions. This leads to ad hoc rollbacks, poorly measured customer impact, and repeated incidents where low-priority traffic is not shed in a controlled manner.
goals: 1) Define precise per-endpoint SLI definitions and leaseable SLO headroom semantics. 2) Implement an automated SLO-lease protocol that allows controlled borrowing and returning of error budget/capacity with guardrails. 3) Define the GTA policy and prioritized eviction order for load shedding. 4) Integrate into the Console (dashboards + audit trail) and runtime control plane for enforcement and observability.
proposed_sli_definitions: We propose the following canonical SLIs to be used in SLO declarations for routes/endpoints: - latency_p95: request-to-last-token latency at 95th percentile (ms) - success_rate: fraction of requests returning valid model response (excluding benign client-side cancels) - kv_cache_hit_rate: proportion of requests benefiting from prefix/KV cache - freshness: proportion of responses generated with the pinned model version (for strict versioned routes) SLI collection must include resource tags (region, model_variant, route_id) so SLOs can be evaluated per endpoint and aggregated for lease calculations.
slo_and_error_budget_semantics: An SLO declaration contains: - objective: e.g., 99.5% success_rate over a 30d rolling window or latency_p95 <= 600ms - baseline_error_budget: computed from objective (1 - objective) * window_volume - leaseable_fraction: percent of baseline_error_budget that can be borrowed (default 20%, configurable per route) - min_reserve: minimum unborrowable headroom to prevent catastrophic borrowing (default 5% of baseline) - priority_tier: integer indicating route priority (1 = highest) Error budgets are evaluated hourly for lease decisions. Leases are timeboxed and must include an auto-expiry and cooldown window.
lease_and_transfer_mechanism: Mechanics: - Lease request: A route that is approaching exhaustion can request a lease from lower-priority routes in the same region or designated regional peers. - Selection: The control plane evaluates candidate donors by available leaseable_fraction and min_reserve, preferring same-tenant donors first, then region-wide donors. - Transfer: A lease is a metadata record that reduces donor route's available error budget and increases borrower available budget; transfer is implemented as a soft policy in runtime traffic routing (e.g., amount of burst capacity, reduced circuit breaker sensitivity). - Timebox: default lease TTL is 15 minutes; renewable up to 3 times with review. - Revocation: donors can opt-out with a manual override (requires SSO approval) or automatic revocation if donor crosses its min_reserve. - Audit: every lease creates an immutable audit event recorded in Console and linked to the route's error-budget timeline.
circuit_breaker_policy: Replace monolithic CBs with hierarchical CBs: - route-level CB: sensitive thresholds for immediate client-visible failures (e.g., sustained error_rate > 3% for 1 min triggers fast-open) - variant-level CB: groups model variants and can preemptively shift traffic at lower thresholds to protect capacity - region-level CB: global protection across routes - lease-aware CB tuning: when a route holds a lease, its route-level CB thresholds are adjusted upward by a lease_scaling_factor (e.g., +20% error threshold) to utilize borrowed headroom without instant tripping. All CB state transitions must be exposed via tracing and Console.
load_shedding_priority_and_gta: Graceful Traffic Atrophy (GTA) defines deterministic shedding order: 1) Non-authenticated public evals / playground (lowest priority) 2) low-value background batch jobs (e.g., non-service user embeddings) 3) free-tier interactive routes 4) paid non-urgent routes 5) paid high-priority / SLA-backed routes (do not shed unless all leases and fallbacks exhausted) Shedding actions (in descending severity): - prefix rejection: fast reject based on route label - degrade model_variant to cheaper quantized variant with SLO-aware thresholds - rate-limit per-client with token-bucket tailored to tier - full reject with 503 and a structured retry-after header The GTA engine must ensure gradual steps with observability for each step taken.
rollout_and_testing: Phases: 1) Simulation: run synthetic traffic using existing incident traces to validate lease selection and GTA ordering. 2) Canary: enable lease protocol in a single non-critical region and a low-risk route. 3) Observability hardening: add dedicated dashboards (per-route lease metrics, donor/borrower events, CB state machine) and an alert for unexpected donor depletion. 4) Gradual expansion to production regions and enforcement on high-priority routes only after 2 weeks of stable metrics. QA: chaos tests (circuit-breaker rapid-fires, donor exhaustion scenario), DR drills (full-region outage) Acceptance criteria: - No increase in end-user error rate for P0 routes during tested spikes - Lease audit trail visible and queryable in Console - GTA shedding steps execute in expected priority order during synthetic overloads
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: - Lease activity: active leases, average TTL, donor/borrower matrices - Error-budget heatmap by route/region - CB transitions timeline - GTA actions and impact by route Alerts: - donor_depleted: donor available leaseable headroom < min_reserve - lease_too_many_renewals: route renewed lease > configured cap - unexpected_cb_open: route-level CB opened without active lease dependencies Must attach event IDs to metrics for post-incident correlation.
risks_and_mitigation: Risks: - donor overcommit leading to donor customer impact - lease metadata corruption - complex cross-region synchronization causing inconsistent enforcement Mitigations: - conservative defaults (20% leaseable, 5% min_reserve) - strong audit + read-after-write verification for lease creation - synchronous revocation fallback path and fail-safe that reverts to regional CBs
acceptance_criteria: - SLI collection works for all targeted routes and tagged by region+variant - Lease creation, renewal, and revocation produce immutable audit events - GTA shedding policy reduces overall system load in synthetic spikes and respects the priority ordering - No P0 route degradation observed in canary and first two regional rollouts
